headline: product-catalog GetProduct calls intermittently rejected by the productCatalogFailure fault-injection flag path in src/product-catalog/main.go, cascading HTTP 500s through cart, recommendations, product pages, and checkout via frontend. Sustained heavy failure 07:56-08:20 UTC then intermittent 5-10 min bursts, last observed burst 09:57 UTC. Since ~10:07 UTC product-catalog has been idle (no traffic, no errors) — no positive recovery evidence, only absence of exercise. RCA is done and verified; incident stays open pending remediation.
blast_radius: During active bursts (07:56-09:57 UTC): every user-facing route depending on product-catalog GetProduct is degraded — product detail pages, cart hydration, recommendations, and checkout. Observed peak error rates ~47% of checkout attempts and ~38-47% of product detail page loads across all 10 catalog product IDs during the initial 07:56-08:20 UTC sustained window. Routes not depending on product-catalog (e.g. /api/data?contextKeys=accessories, ~1.8% failure) unaffected — blast radius bounded to this one dependency's callers. Currently (12:27 UTC): user-visible impact is zero *because there are no users* — load-generator HTTP scenario is not producing requests, so no callers are exercising product-catalog to be blocked; this is not the same as 'the fault is fixed'.
reasoning: Single alert, single root cause, so DECLARE rather than ATTACH/MERGE (nothing else is open) or SPLIT (there's only one causal thread here, not two). Chose sev2 over sev1 because the failure is intermittent and self-recovering between bursts rather than a total unrecovering outage, but it directly hits the revenue-critical checkout path at a high rate during bursts, which rules out sev3/sev4. Status stays 'open' this shift: no new error bursts in the last ~2.5 hours, but also no positive evidence of recovery — product-catalog has essentially zero span traffic since ~10:07 UTC because the loadGeneratorTraffic scenario is not currently generating requests, and flagd's /status endpoint publishes only defaultVariant, not the live variant, so I cannot from here prove the productCatalogFailure flag is off. Silence-without-exercise is exactly the resolution failure mode the base playbook warns against — an alert not firing is not evidence of recovery. Cannot resolve.

revisions.new_evidence: Mimir traces_span_metrics_calls_total per-10m increase for service_name=product-catalog, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, 08:27-12:27 UTC window queried this shift: bursts at 08:27 (533), 08:37 (239), 08:47 (59), 08:57 (180), 09:27 (106), 09:57 (77); zero every bucket since 09:57 UTC. Successful span (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) traffic also fell to zero after 10:07 UTC apart from a 2.2-span blip at 11:07 — the service has essentially been idle since, so 'no errors' is not attributable to recovery. Flagd defaultVariant=off but live variant is not published, so flag state remains unknowable from here.
revisions.now_believes: The incident continued producing bursts for ~1 hour after the prior shift's snapshot (09:57 UTC last observed). Since 10:07 UTC product-catalog has been idle, which prevents any observation of recovery-or-not. Severity unchanged (sev2 — impact when triggered is unchanged; only exercise has stopped). Status stays open.
revisions.why_changed: The prior shift's timeline was correct at time of writing but has been overtaken by later evidence. Silently updating the headline would violate 'silently changing your story is worse than being wrong' — recording it explicitly here.

escalation.observed: 07:56-09:57 UTC intermittent-burst error pattern on product-catalog GetProduct, ~9.5% error rate over the 4h window ending 12:27 UTC (~789 error spans / ~7543 non-error spans); zero errors and near-zero traffic since 10:07 UTC.
escalation.ruled_out: Two independent incidents (only one causal thread — the productCatalogFailure flag path in checkProductFailure, verified). App-log-visible cause (ruled out by log-triage this shift and prior — Loki ERROR streams for product-catalog empty). Cross-service unrelated faults during the same window (frontend/recommendation/cart error span rates all trace back through the same GetProduct dependency).
escalation.open_question: Is the productCatalogFailure flag currently off, or is product-catalog simply not being called? Cannot determine from flagd's /status endpoint (publishes defaultVariant only, not live variant) and cannot determine from metrics/traces (no traffic to observe). Not escalating to a new phase — RCA already done and verified — but flagging the observability gap so remediation and next-shift log-triage know why this stayed open despite ~2.5 quiet hours.

rca.root_cause: product-catalog's GetProduct gRPC handler is gated by checkProductFailure, which evaluates the OpenFeature/flagd boolean flag productCatalogFailure (default false, generated binding flags.ProductCatalogFailure) per-request via a targetless evaluation context keyed on product_id. When the flag evaluates true for a given request, GetProduct returns before ever calling getProductFromDB, setting a gRPC error with code Internal (13) and the literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' -- exactly matching the trace evidence (rpc.grpc.status_code=13, grpc.error_message text) verbatim. Because nearly every user-facing route (product detail, cart, recommendations, checkout) calls GetProduct to hydrate product data, this single upstream fault cascades into HTTP 500s across all of them, which is exactly the blast radius alert-grouping observed. This is the demo's deliberate fault-injection code path executing correctly as designed when the flag is on for a given evaluation, not an accidental bug in the flag-check logic itself -- the bursty on/off pattern reflects the flag being toggled/cycled by the fault scenario, not a malfunction in checkProductFailure.
rca.verify_detail: Two independent blind sub-agent verifications, both CONFIRMED. (1) Original verify at 09:05 UTC: fresh sub-agent given only the bare claim (file src/product-catalog/main.go, function checkProductFailure, called from GetProduct, gRPC code Internal, literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', returned before the DB lookup) independently confirmed via `gh api repos/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/contents/src/product-catalog` that the file exists, then fetched raw content and quoted: GetProduct calling checkProductFailure at line 373; checkProductFailure at lines 419-420 evaluating flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value with a targetless evaluation context keyed on product_id; the error branch at lines 374-377 returning status.Error(codes.Internal, msg) with exact msg match; getProductFromDB reached only afterward at line 380. (2) Re-verify at 12:35 UTC, this shift, triggered by 12:27 UTC revision extending burst timeline through 09:57 UTC: fresh second sub-agent, blind to prior reasoning, re-fetched the same three files (main.go, flags/flags_gen.go, flags.json) directly from raw.githubusercontent.com and re-confirmed every element -- path exists, function exists, exact error string byte-for-byte match on lines 366-378, ordering before getProductFromDB confirmed, flag definitions boolean/default-false confirmed in both flags_gen.go (lines 29-49) and flags.json (lines 3-9). In parallel, a live Tempo query pulled a trace from a newer burst (trace 459602e162bb82e8f75431e7bf07b2d, ~09:50 UTC, well after the original 09:05 RCA and inside the extended 08:27-09:57 UTC burst window described in the 12:27 revision) and directly observed product-catalog GetProduct spans carrying the identical status.message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' -- proving the mechanism did not silently shift mid-incident. Verdict: CONFIRMED, both code-claim verify and newer-burst trace-signature check.

remediation.second_opinion: not solicited — no candidate diff or config change existed to review. Deferred outcome reasoned directly against the verified RCA and the project's hard rules.
remediation.summary: Verified cause is the productCatalogFailure flag's live variant flipped to on, not a code defect. A code_fix removing checkProductFailure would delete a deliberate demo feature (reckless per playbook 'fix the cause, don't hide the symptom'); a config_proposal editing flags.json / demo.flagd.json cannot override a runtime variant (defaultVariant is already off); calling flagd /toggle to reset live state is prohibited by the project's hard rules. Incident stays open. Full rationale at remediations/incident-001/rationale.md.

release_approval.own_re_review: Independently re-fetched src/product-catalog/main.go from raw.githubusercontent.com and confirmed RCA byte-for-byte: GetProduct calls checkProductFailure, on true returns status.Error(codes.Internal, 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled') before getProductFromDB, and checkProductFailure evaluates flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value with a targetless product_id evaluation context — RCA verified independently, not accepted on trust. Then re-reviewed PR #3 (prior run's still-open remediation candidate, branch agent/inc-0001-product-catalog-1786263568657) against the four checks. Check 2 (minimal and scoped to verified cause): fails — the diff adds only runbooks/product-catalog-feature-flag.md, an 18-line new markdown file; it touches no code and no flag config, so nothing about the verified cause changes if this merges. Check 3 (no reckless pattern): fails — the runbook prescribes 'Disable the fail feature flag' as the standard resolution, which is exactly the action that would require calling flagd's /toggle. That action is a hard-ruled prohibition for this SRE ('No capability may call flagd's /toggle — read-only on the real target system's fault-injection state, always', sre-engineer/CLAUDE.md). Merging installs, in the team's repo, guidance that a future responder would reasonably read as sanctioning the prohibited action, and it embeds the exact 'hide the symptom' pattern that this shift's own remediation rationale (remediations/incident-001/rationale.md) identified as reckless for this cause. The runbook also carries no evidence citations — no incident id, no trace id, no code line reference — which is the 'wrong answer stated confidently' pattern personality.md rejects. Check 4 (syntactically valid markdown): passes (missing trailing newline is trivial). Check 1 passes (RCA holds independently). Failing 2 and 3 means merge is not safe.
release_approval.objection: PR #3 adds a runbook advertising 'disable the fail feature flag' as the resolution — an action that, on this system, requires calling flagd's /toggle, which is explicitly prohibited by the project's hard rules (sre-engineer/CLAUDE.md). The diff does not touch the verified implicated file (src/product-catalog/main.go::checkProductFailure) or any flag config, so merging it does not address the RCA-confirmed cause; it only installs contradictory guidance in the repo. This shift's own remediation reached a deferred verdict on the same reasoning — a runbook telling the next responder to reach for the prohibited action directly contradicts that assessment. Rejection stands regardless of the prior-run second opinion; the merge is the irreversible step and this reviewer's four-check verdict is that it is not safe.
